A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Test-time Correlation Alignment with the same authors and core framework. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are accessible and matchable despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark, efficiency, forgetting, theoretical-validation, and synthetic-shift experiments in Sections 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds DomainNet, ImageNet-C, CLIP, nonlinear-transformation, source-access, and batch-size results. Table 5 explicitly distinguishes borrowed baseline results from the work's TCA results.

M1.justification: v2 adds two- and three-layer MLP transformation variants of LinearTCA and LinearTCA+ in Section 5.5 and Table 6. These extend the original linear alignment procedure, while the principal algorithms in Section 4 and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds DomainNet's six-domain, 345-class evaluation, ImageNet-C's 1,000-class corruption evaluation, and VLCS classification within the CLIP experiments. The original PACS, OfficeHome, CIFAR-10-C, CIFAR-100-C, and synthetic-shift coverage is retained.

E2.justification: T3A, AdaNPC, and PLC are added to the existing accuracy, efficiency, and forgetting comparisons and corresponding appendix tables. The new CLIP comparison also includes TPT, CLIPArTT, WATT-P, and WATT-S, with their baseline values explicitly attributed to WATT. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include CLIP-ViT-B/16 comparisons following WATT, target-domain fine-tuning and true-source-distribution controls, and OfficeHome testing across batch sizes 1–1024. DomainNet adds clipart-based hyperparameter selection. The existing default ResNet and ViT batch sizes remain 128 and 64.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of nonlinear transformation depth, performance with true source distributions or target-domain fine-tuning, and batch-size sensitivity of accuracy and pseudo-source estimation error (Tables 6–8). These address questions beyond v1's retained pseudo-source-size, test-sample-size, and synthetic linear/nonlinear-shift analyses.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without empirical uncertainty intervals. v2 Table 5 introduces ± values for the work's LinearTCA+ CLIP results and reproduces uncertainty values for borrowed baselines. The meaning of ± and the run or seed counts remain unspecified.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for the new benchmarks, CLIP comparisons, and Tables 6–8 analyses. On CIFAR-10-C with ViT-B/16, LinearTCA+ remains at 79.55%, but the strongest baseline changes from EATA at 73.67% to AdaNPC at 74.60%, reducing its margin from 5.88 to 4.95 points. Some retained baseline scores and runtime/memory measurements also change; these do not establish same-setting efficiency gains.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.5 and Appendix B.1 substantially revise the probability bound and its Chernoff derivation, introducing source-sample-size dependence and explicitly sampling source instances from Ds intersect Omega. The covariance concentration argument is rewritten to distinguish sampled, true-source, and pseudo-source matrices and specifies a unit-range assumption. Theorem 3.6 and Corollary 3.7 are substantively retained.

C1.justification: The abstract removes v1's specific claim of a 5.88% LinearTCA improvement on OfficeHome and adds a headline CLIP performance claim. The central contributions—source-free correlation alignment, theoretical support, efficient LinearTCA, and plug-and-play LinearTCA+—remain the same.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting CLIP performance to image-text embedding alignment and small-batch robustness to incremental covariance estimation. It also interprets true-source controls as evidence of the importance of approximating source distributions. The existing limitations concerning imperfect pseudo-sources, weak feature extractors, and nonlinear shifts remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies a fixed 1e-3 transformation-optimization learning rate, AdaNPC tuning information, and TorchVision initialization for ImageNet-C. The code link and core implementation description remain unchanged. Conversely, the explicit continual-corruption order and associated caption wording are removed, reducing protocol documentation without establishing that the underlying procedure changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting T3A, PLC, WATT, CLIP, DomainNet, and probabilistic contrastive TTA, and expands Appendix A's descriptions of selected comparators. The CORAL positioning and distinction between backpropagation-free and backpropagation-based methods were already present in v1 and remain intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, parts of the introduction, and efficiency, forgetting, and ablation discussions receive localized rewrites. A foundation-model subsection is inserted before the expanded analysis section, while the overall narrative and Appendix A–E organization remain stable.

P2.justification: Table 1 is substantially reorganized into separate domain and corruption blocks with method categories; Table 2 combines its memory and runtime displays. Figure 1 adds comparator traces, Tables 5–8 introduce new main-text displays, and the appendix gains benchmark tables and comparator rows. The original pipeline and diagnostic figures are retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evaluation of the central efficiency and applicability claims by adding directly relevant backpropagation-free comparators, larger-scale and CLIP evaluations, and tests of nonlinear alignment and small-batch behavior. These address important evidential gaps in v1. The gains outweigh reporting problems: Section 5.3 overstates LinearTCA's DomainNet ranking relative to Table 1, and Table 7 uses unexplained OfficeHome reference scores that differ from the main comparison.
